reference: GNU coreutils mv from the isolated runner PATH; the metadata contract is grounded in Bash type/help builtins and the mv documentation in the source.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and help metadata
Quoted relative paths and binary file contents
Force overwrite, no-clobber, and interactive EOF behavior
Additional bounded regular-file, hardlink, symlink and multi-operand error continuation regressions.
exclusions: EXDEV copy-and-remove fallback is deferred because the fixture runner exposes only one writable filesystem tree; exercising it needs a disposable environment with two distinct writable filesystems or a reviewed EXDEV syscall mock.
Interactive tests use EOF and bounded here-strings; real PTY behavior is not qualified.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports mv as a builtin and exposes its documented synopsis and no-clobber help text.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t mv) == builtin ]] || exit 1
h=$(help mv) || exit 1
[[ $h == *"SRC... DST"* && $h == *"-n   no-clobber: never overwrite"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin help contract
'

cases.purpose: Move a relative file with spaces and embedded NUL bytes using --; GNU mv is the independent behavior oracle and the tree comparison checks exact bytes and source removal.
Move multiple relative sources into a directory with -t, including an operand beginning with a dash after --; GNU mv supplies status and filesystem expectations.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'alpha\n' > alpha
printf 'dash\n' > -beta
mv -t destination -- alpha -beta

cases.purpose: Check -f replaces an existing regular destination with source bytes and removes the source; GNU mv is the independent oracle.
cases.script:
printf 'new contents\n' > source
printf 'old contents\n' > destination
mv -f source destination

cases.purpose: Check -n leaves an existing destination untouched and retains the skipped source; GNU mv determines the reference exit status.
cases.script:
printf 'source bytes\n' > source
printf 'destination bytes\n' > destination
mv -n source destination

cases.purpose: With the runner's /dev/null stdin, check that -i declines an overwrite at EOF and compare GNU mv's status, prompt presence, and resulting tree.
cases.script:
printf 'source bytes\n' > source
printf 'destination bytes\n' > destination
mv -i source destination

cases.purpose: Move a symlink without following it and preserve its relative target while leaving the referent unchanged; GNU mv is the independent oracle.
cases.script:
printf 'referent bytes\n' > referent
ln -s referent link
mv link moved-link

cases.purpose: Moving a file onto itself must fail with a diagnostic and preserve the file contents, matching GNU mv.
cases.script:
printf 'preserve me\n' > same
mv same same

cases.purpose: -T forces the destination to be treated as one path; a regular source must not be moved inside an existing directory, matching GNU mv's error and unchanged tree.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'source\n' > source
mv -T source destination

cases.purpose: A missing source must fail with a diagnostic and leave the fixture tree unchanged, matching GNU mv.
Exercise the cross-device fallback for regular files, symlinks, and directory trees while comparing GNU mv and preserving source metadata.
Bounded here-strings exercise affirmative and negative prompt responses without a PTY.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
if mv -i source target <<< n; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if mv -i source target <<< y; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"

cases.purpose: Moving between two hardlinks to the same inode must fail and preserve both names.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln source alias
mv source alias

cases.purpose: A regular move replaces the destination symlink and leaves its referent and hardlink unchanged.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
ln target hard
ln -s target alias
mv source alias

cases.purpose: A missing middle operand must not prevent later operands from moving.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf first > first
printf last > last
mv first absent last destination

cases.purpose: An EOF refusal should set failure while a later non-colliding source is still moved.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf new > first
printf old > destination/first
printf last > last
mv -i first last destination

cases.purpose: Check existing last -f/-i/-n wins precedence and skipped symlink destinations.
cases.script:
printf a > a
printf b > b
printf c > c
printf old > target
ln -s target alias
mv -fn a alias
mv -nf b target
if mv -ni c target; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf '%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: No-clobber skips existing destinations only for valid sources; a missing source still fails and later operands continue.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf old > destination/absent
printf last > last
mv -n absent last destination

cases.purpose: Rename a private nonempty directory preserving nested content, permissions and hardlink identity.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub
printf 'payload\000end' > source/sub/file
ln source/sub/file source/alias
chmod 750 source
mv source renamed
